source.title: The Li–Lin’s open problem on R^N

accepted.question_text: For an integer N ≥ 3, let Ω be a smooth bounded domain in R^N, let 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, let λ > 0, and define the Hardy–Sobolev critical exponent 2*(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2) for 0 ≤ s ≤ 2. For parameters 2 < p ≤ 2*(s1) and 2 < q ≤ 2*(s2), does the zero-Dirichlet Hardy–Sobolev equation −Δu = −λ |x|^(−s1) |u|^(p−2)u + |x|^(−s2) |u|^(q−2)u in Ω, with u = 0 on ∂Ω, admit positive solutions in the Li–Lin regime s1 < s2 and λ > 0, particularly in the difficult case p > q and especially p > q = 2*(s2)?

evidence.quote: In 2012, Y.Y. Li and C.-S. Lin (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal., 203 (3): 943–968) posed an open problem concerning the existence of positive solutions to the elliptic equation { −∆u = −λ|x|−s1 |u|p−2u + |x|−s2 |u|q−2u in Ω, u = 0 on ∂Ω, for λ > 0, p > q = 2∗(s2), 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, and 2∗(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2) denotes the Hardy-Sobolev critical exponent, initially studied in bounded domains Ω ⊂ RN, N ≥ 3. Currently, research on this open problem remains limited, and a complete resolution is still far from being achieved.

Consider the following nonlinear equation involving Hardy-Sobolev exponents: { −∆u = −λ|x|−s1 |u|p−2u + |x|−s2 |u|q−2u in Ω, u(x) = 0 on ∂Ω, (1.1) where ∆ denotes the standard Laplace operator, Ω is a smooth bounded domain in RN (N ≥ 3), λ ∈ R, 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, 2∗(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2) for 0 ≤ s ≤ 2, 2 < p ≤ 2∗(s1), and 2 < q ≤ 2∗(s2).

However, when λ > 0 and p > q, (PS)c sequences may not be bounded, making it difficult to obtain satisfactory results. Y.Y. Li and C.-S. Lin [8] identified this challenge in their research and posed the following open problem: When s1 < s2 and λ > 0, the existence of positive solutions to equation (1.1) remains completely unknown.

accepted.question_text: For an integer N ≥ 3, let Ω be a smooth bounded domain in R^N and let 0 < s < 2. With Hardy–Sobolev critical exponent 2*(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2), and with exponent p satisfying 2*(s) − 1 < p < (N + 2)/(N − 2), does the Dirichlet elliptic problem Δu − u^p + u^(2*(s)−1)/|x|^s = 0 in Ω, with u = 0 on ∂Ω, admit positive solutions?

evidence.quote: Consider the following nonlinear equation involving Hardy-Sobolev exponents: { −∆u = −λ|x|−s1 |u|p−2u + |x|−s2 |u|q−2u in Ω, u(x) = 0 on ∂Ω, (1.1) where ∆ denotes the standard Laplace operator, Ω is a smooth bounded domain in RN (N ≥ 3), λ ∈ R, 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, 2∗(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2) for 0 ≤ s ≤ 2, 2 < p ≤ 2∗(s1), and 2 < q ≤ 2∗(s2).
Specifically, for the equation ∆u − up + u2∗(s)−1/|x|s = 0 in Ω, where 0 < s < 2 and 2∗(s) − 1 < p < (N + 2)/(N − 2), the existence of positive solutions remains an interesting open problem.

accepted.question_text: For an integer N ≥ 3, let 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, λ > 0, and 2*(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2). For the whole-space Hardy–Sobolev equation −Δu + u = −λ |x|^(−s1) |u|^(p−2)u + |x|^(−s2) |u|^(q−2)u in R^N, determine whether nonzero or positive solutions exist in the critical regime 2*(s2) = q < p ≤ 2*(s1), and in the subcritical regime 2 < q < p < 2*(s1), q < 2*(s2), with q > ((2 − s2)/(2 − s1))p + (2s2 − 2s1)/(2 − s1).
accepted.context_brief: Whole-space extension of the Li–Lin problem

evidence.quote: Motivated by resolving this open problem in more general settings, we aim to analyze how the equation’s solutions behave when the domain is an unbounded region, particularly RN. Now, we consider the Hardy-Sobolev’s critical exponents problem −∆u + u = −λ|x|−s1 |u|p−2u + |x|−s2 |u|q−2u in RN, (1.2) where N ≥ 3, λ ∈ R, 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, 2∗(s) = 2(N − s)/(N − 2) for 0 ≤ s ≤ 2, 2 < p ≤ 2∗(s1), 2 < q ≤ 2∗(s2).
Specifically, in RN, for any λ > 0, the equation has no solution when q = 2∗(s2), while it has a solution when q < 2∗(s2).
Theorem 1.1 Suppose that 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2 and 2∗(s2) = q < p ≤ 2∗(s1). Then Problem (1.2) has no nonzero solution for all λ > 0.

Theorem 1.3 Suppose that 0 ≤ s1 < s2 < 2, 2 < q < p < 2∗(s1) and q < 2∗(s2). Assume that q > ((2 − s2)/(2 − s1))p + (2s2 − 2s1)/(2 − s1). Then Problem (1.2) has at least one positive solution for all λ > 0.
